title: Ethics & Relationships: Foundations
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the key terms for marriage, family and relationships in Christianity and Islam.
meta_desc: GCSE RS Relationships foundations — marriage, family, cohabitation and key vocabulary.
final_note: You now know the foundational vocabulary for ethics and relationships.

concepts.def: A legal/religious union, usually for life, often before God
Living together as a couple without being married
Two parents and their dependent children
Family including grandparents, aunts, uncles, cousins
Sexual relations with someone other than one's spouse
Having children — a traditional purpose of marriage

walkthroughs.body_html:
Christian marriage is a lifelong covenant — 'What God has joined together, let no one separate' (Mark 10:9).

Purposes: love, faithfulness, procreation, mutual support.

Catholics regard marriage as a sacrament; most Protestants see it as a sacred covenant rather than a sacrament.

In Islam marriage (nikah) is a contract before Allah and witnesses, strongly encouraged for adult Muslims.

The Qur'an describes spouses as 'garments for one another' (2:187).

Faithfulness and family life are central duties.

Family types include nuclear, extended, single-parent, same-sex and blended families.

Christianity traditionally teaches parents should raise children in faith (Proverbs 22:6). Islam teaches strong respect for parents — 'Lower the wing of humility' to them (Qur'an 17:24).

mcqs.q: What is the doctrine of the Trinity?
options: The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.
God is one being existing in three persons (Father, Son, Holy Spirit) — distinct in person but united in essence; Christians remain monotheistic.
The Buddha created the universe.
Christians believe in three different gods.

mcqs.q: What do orthodox Christians believe about the nature of Jesus?
options: Jesus was a human who became God after his resurrection.
Jesus was half God and half human.
The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.
He is fully God and fully human at the same time (the incarnation) — both natures united in one person, as defined at the Council of Chalcedon.

mcqs.q: Is the Buddha a god in Buddhism?
options: The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.
The Buddha created the universe.
Buddhists worship the Buddha as their god.

No — the Buddha (Siddhartha Gautama) is regarded as an enlightened human teacher who discovered the path to liberation. Theravada Buddhism is generally non-theistic; some Mahayana traditions develop more elaborate cosmologies.
